subject: Clarify: 'Special Damages' carve-out language & next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify: 'Special Damages' carve-out language & next steps

Samir —

Thanks for the redline. We reviewed the MSA changes overnight. Two narrow asks from our side on the damages carve-outs so we can finalize (and surface to finance/legal on our end):

1) Definition clarity: the term "Special Damages" is used in three places and appears to be trying to capture both indirect/consequential losses and certain third-party claim recoveries. Can you confirm whether ACME intends the term to include (a) lost profits, (b) loss of business/reputation, and (c) third-party claims for product failures?

2) Mutuality vs one-way: ACME's proposed one-way exclusion for consequential losses shifts significant exposure to Redwood. We're open to a one-way exclusion for consequential losses if ACME will accept a mutual carve-out for incidental/punitive-type losses and agree to a narrow exception for: (i) confidentiality/PII breaches, and (ii) direct third-party claims arising from ACME's integration of non-Redwood software (where ACME controls the integration).

Attached is a brief annotated redline (Acme_MSA_redline_v4.docx) with our proposed phrasing and a short list of examples that show what would/wouldn't be excluded under the narrower definition.

Proposed next steps: if this reads OK to you, can we set a 30-min call Tuesday to land final language? If you'd prefer, we can push a short compromise snippet via DocuSign for signature after legal sync.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Mobile: (415) 555-0198

Attachment: Acme_MSA_redline_v4.docx (document with inline comments)

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Johnson <m.johnson@acme.com>, ACME Legal <contracts@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: 'Special Damages' carve-out language & next steps

Ben —

Appreciate the swift read. Brief answers first then a couple questions:

On definition: ACME's intent was to have consequential damages cover foreseeable downstream losses including lost profits and lost business value that directly flow from a service outage. We did not mean to sweep in third-party claim recoveries (we agree that's a separate bucket), but the current draft conflates them.

On mutuality: ACME's commercial team pushed for one-way because of our regulatory posture in certain contracts with our customers — we cannot contractually cap certain downstream liabilities in those cases. That said, we understand Redwood's concern.

Two questions before we lock a call:
- Can Redwood accept a mutual exclusion for 'punitive' and 'incidental' but keep 'consequential' one-way if we add a definition that explicitly limits consequential to "foreseeable losses resulting from ACME's direct use of the Service" and excludes third-party claim recoveries?
- Would Redwood accept an exception to the exclusion for confidentiality/PII damages without a separate unlimited liability bucket — e.g., carve out such damages up to a multiple of the contract value (ACME is open to a reasonable cap).

We can do Tuesday 11am PT — works for Maya and me. CCing contracts.

—Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Commercial Contracts
Acme Corp.
contracts@acme.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 08:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: 'Special Damages' carve-out language & next steps

Samir — thanks. Quick internal summary and proposed compromise so the call is productive:

Summary of positions
- ACME: wants consequential one-way; willing to define consequential narrowly; open to cap on confidentiality damages
- Redwood: wants mutual exclusions for indirect/incidental/punitive; open to tailored carve-outs for PII/confidentiality and third-party claims where ACME controls integration

Proposed compromise (one-paragraph redline — pasted below):
"Except for damages arising from (i) Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct, (ii) actual unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Confidential Information, and (iii) third-party claims to the extent caused by Customer's modifications or integrations of the Service, neither party shall be liable for incidental, special, consequential or punitive damages, including lost profits, loss of business, or loss of goodwill. "

Key clarifications to include in the definitions:
- "Consequential damages" = foreseeable downstream economic losses directly resulting from the non-availability of the Service; does not include third-party claim recoveries or statutory fines.
- "Third-party claims" = claims by a party not a signatory to this Agreement; carve-out applies only where the signatory's integration/configuration (not Redwood's Service) is the proximate cause.

On confidentiality/PII: we accept an exception but propose a capped bucket equal to 3x the annual contract value for confidentiality-related direct damages (not unlimited). If ACME prefers a different multiple, let's surface that on the call.

If that looks reasonable, I'll send a short DocuSign-ready snippet post-call so we can close the loop and get commercial signed. Call confirmed for Tue 11am PT.

Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarify: 'Special Damages' carve-out language & next steps

All —

Thanks for the draft language, Ben. ACME can work with the proposed paragraph with two requests before we sign: (1) we would like the confidentiality/PII exception to be uncapped where a breach is the result of Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct; and (2) for other confidentiality harms, we are willing to accept the 3x ACV cap but ask that statutory fines (e.g., GDPR/CCPA penalties) be explicitly excluded from that cap.

If Redwood accepts those two points, contracting team will prepare a final redline and send a DocuSign link. We have a short internal review window but expect to get that over to you by end of day Wednesday.

Maya
